approved: Biosecurity Amendment (Clarifying Conditionally Non-prohibited Goods) Bill 2021
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would confirm that certain biosecurity determinations are legally valid despite any technical defects in how they were made.
It would retrospectively validate determinations made under subsection 174(1) of the Biosecurity Act 2015 that specify goods as conditionally non-prohibited.
The bill does not alter any conditions or categories of goods, nor does it create new ones.
Validates determinations made under subsection 174(1) of the Biosecurity Act 2015.
Ensures these determinations are taken to have always been valid.
Confirms that goods specified in the determinations are conditionally non-prohibited goods.
The Director of Biosecurity, the Director of Human Biosecurity, and the Agriculture Minister are affected, along with importers of goods covered by the determinations.

The Labor speaker announced support for the Biosecurity Amendment Bill to correct drafting errors but criticised the Morrison government's biosecurity mismanagement, citing the axing of a recommended biosecurity levy, the delivery of only 2,600 of 25,000 promised agricultural workers, and $45 million in dumped produce; they moved a second reading amendment to note ongoing government inaction.

The Biosecurity Amendment (Clarifying Conditionally Non-prohibited Goods) Bill 2021 confirms the validity of existing determinations under section 174 of the Biosecurity Act 2015 for conditionally non-prohibited goods and their conditions, without creating or changing any classes of goods, to maintain effective biosecurity risk management.
